headline: Network and enrichment frameworks for microbial, metabolomic and disease gene data
label: Computational Network And Enrichment Methods
summary: Recent work extends network and enrichment frameworks to differential microbial, drug repurposing and metabolomic analyses across disease datasets.
synthesis: The dominant thread is network-structured or set-based inference applied to differential molecular profiles, where the unit of analysis is a relation among genes, proteins, metabolites or microbial gene families rather than a single feature. A differential microbial gene-family network with pathway enrichment is applied to IBD, diabetes and atherosclerosis stratified by sex. RepurNet screens compounds against reverse disease gene signatures and builds protein-interaction disease modules, while the cancer preprint proposes a quantitative dynamical model over gene deregulation networks to predict bidirectional phenotype reversal. iDMET+ extends metabolite-set enrichment by using differential metabolomic profiles as the sets, validated on renal, colorectal and small cell lung cancer. What is new is the transfer of differential-network and enrichment logic to these data types, though the items are heterogeneous and only the microbial item addresses microbial data directly.
